status.nb: 15 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 25 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Baghdad, Kirkuk og Erbil.

summary.en: Iraqi authorities are disarming PKK-linked Yazidi militias, including YBŞ and YJŞ, and integrating them into the army and interior ministry while pledging to protect Yazidi rights and Mount Shengal. The intelligence chief Hamid al-Shatri was removed, a court ordered the arrest of the Maysan provincial council chief for defying Iran’s border closure, and parliament approved most remaining cabinet posts, some held by Iran-backed militia figures. A vessel caught fire off Iraq’s Al-Faw coast and Iraqi forces seized more than two tons of drugs in 2026. The conflict produced 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Irakiske myndigheter avvæpner PKK-tilknyttede yezidmilitser, inkludert YBŞ og YJŞ, og integrerer dem i hæren og innenriksdepartementet mens de lover å beskytte yezidrettighetene og Mount Shengal. Etterretningsoverlegen Hamid al-Shatri ble fjernet, en domstol beordret arrestasjon av lederen for Maysan provinsråd for å ha trosset Irans grenselukking, og parlamentet godkjente de fleste gjenværende regjeringspostene, noen holdt av Iran-støttede militsfigurer. Et fartøy tok fyr utenfor Al-Faw-kysten i Irak, og irakiske styrker beslagla mer enn to tonn narkotika i 2026. Konflikten førte til 396 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Iraqi conflict
background.extract: The Iraqi conflict is a series of violent events that began with the 2003 American-led invasion of Iraq and deposition of Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein, followed by a series of conflicts including the protracted Iraq War (2003–2011), the Iraqi insurgency (2011–2013), the War in Iraq (2013–2017), and most recently, the small-scale Islamic State insurgency in 4 provinces located in Northern Iraq since 2017.
